Which issue does this PR close?

  • Closes Optimized decoding of Parquet Statistics, null_pages and null_counts #9296.

Rationale for this change

Today, getting page-level statistics as Arrow arrays copies the data twice:

  • decode_column_index reads the Thrift bytes into ThriftColumnIndex.
  • PrimitiveColumnIndex::try_new then copies the mins and maxes into typed Vec<T>s, putting default values in place for null pages.
  • data_page_mins, data_page_maxes, data_page_null_counts and data_page_nan_counts go through that ColumnIndexMetaData again and push each value into an Arrow builder one at a time.
  • Each call walks the index separately.

What changes are included in this PR?

This PR adds a way to skip loading the column index, then decode only the columns you need straight into Arrow arrays.

New API

pub struct DataPageStatistics {
    pub mins: ArrayRef,
    pub maxes: ArrayRef,
    pub null_counts: UInt64Array,
    pub nan_counts: UInt64Array,
}

impl StatisticsConverter<'_> {
    pub fn data_page_statistics_from_bytes<'b, I>(&self, column_indexes: I) -> Result<DataPageStatistics>
    where I: IntoIterator<Item = (usize, Option<&'b [u8]>)>;
}
  • Input: one (num_pages, bytes) pair per row group. The bytes are the column chunk's serialized ColumnIndex, found with ColumnChunkMetaData::column_index_range(). To avoid parsing the index when the metadata is loaded, load with PageIndexPolicy::Skip.
  • Output: one call returns all four arrays, matching data_page_mins, data_page_maxes, data_page_null_counts and data_page_nan_counts.
  • Missing data: a row group with None bytes, or a column that isn't in the Parquet file, gives num_pages nulls in all four arrays.

The decoder is parquet/src/arrow/arrow_reader/statistics/page_index.rs. It reads the Thrift compact encoding of ColumnIndex in one pass, on top of ThriftSliceInputProtocol.

Field Thrift type Handling
1 null_pages list<bool> Stored one byte per element (0x01 = true; 0x00 and 0x02 = false; any other byte is an error). Inverted to "page has a min/max" and packed into the NullBuffer shared by mins and maxes.
2 min_values, 3 max_values list<binary> Each element is decoded straight into a buffer of the column's physical type (see below). The bytes of null pages are skipped without being checked.
4 boundary_order i32 Read and checked, then discarded.
5 null_counts, 8 nan_counts list<i64> Zigzag varints decoded into Vec<u64>. A negative count is an error. A row group without the list gives null entries.
6, 7 level histograms, and unknown fields any Skipped. For integer lists, skipping just counts the bytes whose top bit is clear, which is much faster than decoding each varint.

Physical type to buffer:

Physical type Buffer How each value is decoded
BOOLEAN Vec<bool> First byte ≠ 0
INT32 Vec<i32> First 4 bytes, little-endian
INT64 Vec<i64> First 8 bytes, little-endian
FLOAT Vec<f32> First 4 bytes, little-endian
DOUBLE Vec<f64> First 8 bytes, little-endian
BYTE_ARRAY / FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY read as Decimal32/64/128/256 Vec<i32> … Vec<i256> Big-endian two's complement, sign-extended while reading (from_bytes_to_i*). There is no intermediate BinaryArray. A value must be 1 to 4/8/16/32 bytes long.
Other BYTE_ARRAY / FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY i32 offsets + Vec<u8> → BinaryArray Bytes copied as they are. Fixed-length values are kept as variable-length because a stored min or max may have been truncated.
INT96 Count only Each value is checked to be at least 12 bytes. The result is always nulls, as before.

As in the old decoder, a fixed-width value with extra trailing bytes is accepted, and one with too few bytes is an error with the same message: error converting value, expected N bytes got M.

Benchmark

Benchmarks can be found here #11287. These numbers are from the benchmark run #11285 (comment).

Type Pages full page index (main) from bytes (branch) Speedup
Int64 2,000 37.9 ± 0.04 µs 8.0 ± 0.05 µs 4.7×
Int64 10,000 156.4 ± 0.15 µs 30.6 ± 0.03 µs 5.1×
Utf8 2,000 85.4 ± 0.10 µs 24.6 ± 0.18 µs 3.5×
Utf8 10,000 379.1 ± 0.28 µs 108.2 ± 0.56 µs 3.5×
Utf8View 2,000 89.8 ± 0.12 µs 34.3 ± 0.18 µs 2.6×
Utf8View 10,000 404.9 ± 1.27 µs 154.7 ± 0.66 µs 2.6×
Decimal128(20, 2) 2,000 65.4 ± 0.12 µs 31.8 ± 0.08 µs 2.1×
Decimal128(20, 2) 10,000 284.9 ± 0.30 µs 147.9 ± 0.30 µs 1.9×

Are these changes tested?

  • Unit tests in page_index.rs:
    • Every physical type is compared against every Arrow type with the existing route.
    • Specific tests cover INT96, all-null pages, zero pages, no row groups, a column missing from the file, unknown fields and histograms, and mins stored before null_pages.
  • parquet/tests/arrow_reader/statistics.rs now also checks every existing page-level case through data_page_statistics_from_bytes, using the column index bytes read from the file.

Are there any user-facing changes?

Yes. This PR adds a new public API but nothing existing changes.

  • New method StatisticsConverter::data_page_statistics_from_bytes.
  • New struct parquet::arrow::arrow_reader::statistics::DataPageStatistics.

# Which issue does this PR close?

- Part of #9296.
- Pre-requisite for #11285

# Rationale for this change

I'm planning a [PR]( #11285) that
decodes the stored `ColumnIndex` bytes straight into Arrow arrays,
skipping the intermediate `ColumnIndexMetaData`.

This is the baseline benchmark for this [PR](
#11285).

For page pruning, DataFusion's `page_filter.rs` asks
`StatisticsConverter` for the data page mins, maxes and null counts of
every row group it scans. Each request goes through the fully parsed
`ColumnIndexMetaData`, so the column index is decoded into `Vec`s first
and then copied into Arrow arrays.

# What changes are included in this PR?

A new `page_index_benchmark` group in
`parquet/benches/arrow_statistics.rs`:

- Writes an in-memory file with 20 row groups, 10 rows per data page and
page-level statistics, with every 7th value null.
- Covers `Int64`, `Utf8`, `Utf8View` and `Decimal128(20, 2)`, each with
2,000 and 10,000 data pages in total.
- Reads each row group's raw column index bytes (via
`column_index_range()`) and, inside the timed loop, does what
DataFusion's page pruning effectively does today: `decode_column_index`
→ `PageIndexBuilder` →
`StatisticsConverter::data_page_{mins,maxes,null_counts,nan_counts}`.

# Are these changes tested?

No. 

# Are there any user-facing changes?

No.

mkleen and others added 8 commits September 30, 2026 09:07
feat(parquet): decode ColumnIndex bytes straight into Arrow arrays
5357c90 
Add `StatisticsConverter::data_page_statistics_from_bytes`, which reads the
raw Thrift `ColumnIndex` bytes of each row group and returns the page mins,
maxes, null counts and NaN counts as Arrow arrays in one pass, without first
building `ColumnIndexMetaData`. Callers can skip parsing the column index at
load time (`PageIndexPolicy::Skip`) and decode only the columns they need.

The decoder lives in the arrow reader, so `ParquetMetaData` and
`ColumnIndexMetaData` stay free of Arrow types. INT96 falls back to the
existing `decode_column_index` path. Results match `data_page_mins`,
`data_page_maxes`, `data_page_null_counts` and `data_page_nan_counts`; the
existing statistics integration tests now check both paths, and new unit
tests compare them across all physical/Arrow type pairs.

Benchmark (2000 pages, raw bytes to arrays): Int64 1.64x, Utf8 2.81x,
Decimal128 1.42x faster than decode_column_index + data_page_*.

Part of apache#9296.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
refactor(parquet): decode INT96 page index directly, drop fallback
5b9b407 
`data_page_statistics_from_bytes` no longer falls back to
`decode_column_index` for INT96 columns. No Arrow type is read from INT96
min/max values, so the decoder now only length-checks them (with the same
error as before) and returns null mins/maxes, while null and NaN counts go
through the normal path. The old-path helper moves into the unit tests,
where it remains the reference the new decoder is compared against.

Note that, unlike `data_page_null_counts` / `data_page_nan_counts`, the new
path returns an error for negative null or NaN counts.

The page index benchmark now includes `data_page_nan_counts` in the
baseline, so both sides produce the same four arrays, and adds a
10000-page size. Speed-up over decode_column_index + data_page_*:

  Int64       2000 pages 1.76x, 10000 pages 1.58x
  Utf8        2000 pages 2.72x, 10000 pages 2.65x
  Decimal128  2000 pages 1.39x, 10000 pages 1.30x

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
perf(parquet): decode byte-stored decimal page stats directly
7790650 
When a BYTE_ARRAY or FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY column is read as
Decimal32/64/128/256 (including as a dictionary value type), the page
index decoder now turns each min/max into the decimal number while
reading, instead of copying the bytes into a temporary BinaryArray and
converting in a second pass. Each value type's read loop is kept in its
own non-inlined function so the larger decoder does not slow the other
types down.

The shared `from_bytes_to_i32`..`from_bytes_to_i256` helpers are marked
`#[inline]`: with a second caller, they stopped being inlined into the
existing `data_page_*` conversion code, which made the unchanged old path
~17% slower for Utf8 in benchmarks.

Speed-up of data_page_statistics_from_bytes over decode_column_index +
data_page_* built from main:

  Int64       2000 pages 1.90x, 10000 pages 1.68x
  Utf8        2000 pages 2.76x, 10000 pages 2.65x
  Decimal128  2000 pages 2.47x, 10000 pages 2.37x

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
refactor(parquet): simplify page index statistics decoder
5cb5651 
- `PhysicalValues::finish` returns an `ArrayRef` directly, removing the
  parallel `PhysicalArray` enum. `physical_to_logical` dispatches on the
  physical type to `int32_to_logical`, `int64_to_logical` and
  `bytes_to_logical`.
- `ColumnIndexDecoder::finish` takes the Arrow type and returns
  `DataPageStatistics`, removing `DecodedPageStatistics` and `into_arrow`.
- Merge `read_fixed` into `read_each` and drop `append_null`.
- Shorten the `data_page_statistics_from_bytes` docs and drop its example.
- Deduplicate the mins/maxes writer in the `TestIndex` test helper.

Benchmarks are unchanged within noise.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
refactor(parquet): simplify PhysicalValues and page index decoder
857de89 
- Read deferred min/max lists (stored before null_pages) with the same
  read_list path, dropping append_value and the held-back buffers
- Use read_each for Boolean and INT96 too
- Convert to the logical type in PhysicalValues::finish, removing
  physical_to_logical and the ArrayRef downcasts
- Unwrap dictionary types once; ColumnIndexDecoder::finish takes no args
- Hold mins/maxes as a pair and null/NaN counts in a Counts struct

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix(parquet): error on wrong-length decimal page stats instead of pan…
79b3f72 
…icking

A BYTE_ARRAY or FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY min/max read as a decimal was passed
straight to from_bytes_to_i32..i256, whose sign_extend_be panics on an
empty value or one wider than the decimal. data_page_statistics_from_bytes
runs on raw file bytes, so check the length first and return
"ColumnIndex decimal value has L bytes, expected 1 to N". The existing
metadata path still panics on such values.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
perf(parquet): build view-typed page stats without copying strings
9001885 
Utf8View and BinaryView page statistics were collected value by value,
copying every string longer than 12 bytes into a new buffer and checking
UTF-8 per value. Build the views over the existing byte buffer instead,
validating UTF-8 once as for Utf8. About 2x faster for Utf8View, and
adds a Utf8View case to the page index benchmark.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
perf(parquet): speed up hot loops in the page index decoder
3b16710 
Profiling showed most time in per-value loops. Changes:

- Read fixed-width mins/maxes directly when the stored length matches,
  writing into a pre-sized slice instead of pushing.
- Decode null/NaN counts 8 at a time when each fits in one byte.
- Skip level histograms 8 bytes at a time.
- Validate null_pages flags in one pass, then convert, so both vectorize.
- Check byte array offsets fit in i32 once per list, not per value.

New route vs before: Int64 -56 to -60%, Decimal128 -22%, Utf8 -14%,
Utf8View -11%. Adds tests for long histograms, long count lists and a
negative count within an 8-count group.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
